fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Poll
fields.features_subheading: Describe the poll once, and Emergent builds the page voters see, the table that stores each vote, and the results view.
fields.feature_1:
A poll drafted from one sentence

Describe the poll you want, such as a this-or-that question for Monday's standup. Emergent writes the question and its answer options, and a follow-up prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

Voters open the link and see one question with large answer buttons, sized for a phone. Emergent sets no cap on how many people answer, so a poll can go to a whole company.
fields.feature_3:
Every vote saved in a database you own

Each vote is a row in a database you own, stamped with the poll, the answer, and the time. Compare this month's poll of the day results with last month's whenever you like.
fields.feature_4:
Results that move while people vote

The results page shows bars that update live as votes arrive, and a speaker can put it on screen mid-talk. Hide the totals until the poll closes if early votes would sway others.
fields.feature_5:
Polls posted where your team already talks

Connect Slack, and the app posts each new poll to the channel you pick, then posts the result when it closes. Anyone who has not voted can get an email reminder before the deadline.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Run the poll on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the poll app for next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Polls and What Their Votes Decided
fields.tab_content_1:
Coffee beats tea 22 to 14 by noon

At 9:00 each morning, Pellworth Freight's operations team gets one this-or-that question in Slack. Tuesday's was coffee or tea. By noon, 36 of the 48 people on the team had voted, and coffee won 22 to 14. The app posted the result back to Slack and saved the votes beside every earlier poll of the day.
fields.tab_content_2:
Bowling, with 11 of 24 votes

Ostley Dental Group closes on a Friday each summer for a staff outing, and the staff pick it. The office manager's multiple choice poll takes one vote per person on the staff list, and 24 of 27 staff voted. Bowling got 11 votes, the escape room 7, a cooking class 4, and karaoke 2. She booked the bowling alley that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_3:
Votes from 142 phones fill the slide

The Keswin Ops Summit speaker opens with a QR code and a funny poll question: which is worse, a reply-all storm or a 7 a.m. meeting? People vote on their phones, each question on its own screen, and the bars on her slide grow as votes arrive. Of 180 in the room, 142 voted, and 97 picked the reply-all storm.
fields.tab_content_4:
The cabin wins once all 12 friends vote

Wrenna Brisco sends her 12 friends a would you rather poll for their September trip: a cabin by the lake or a beach house? The day before the deadline, 2 friends still had not voted, and each got an email reminder. Both voted that evening. The cabin won 7 to 5, and Wrenna booked it.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Good Poll Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write poll questions that get votes and a clear winner, then run the poll with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the result will change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle what the poll is for before you write it. A poll of the day only needs to be fun, but a poll that picks an outing or a menu needs a date when you act on the winner. Write that date down first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put a single idea in each question. Coffee or tea gets a clean count. Add hot or iced to the same question, and the room splits four ways with no clear winner. If you need both answers, run two polls on two days.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give a this-or-that poll two answers and a multiple choice poll no more than five. Keep the options the same kind of thing, such as four outings, and add an Other box only if you plan to read what people type.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Joke about shared pain, such as early meetings, reply-all storms, or the office coffee, and never about a person or a group. Read each funny question aloud, picture the quietest person on the team hearing it, and cut any that would sting.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Type one sentence, such as a this-or-that poll for my team's Slack channel at 9:00 each morning, closing at noon. Emergent builds the poll from it. Add who may vote and where the result goes in a follow-up prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link to 3 people before anyone else sees it. Check that each answer reads clearly on a phone, that a second vote from the same person is handled the way you planned, and that the result lands where you expect.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Close on time and act on the winner
fields.howto_step_7_des: Close the poll at the time you announced and post the count with the winning answer. Then do what the poll decided within the week, and say what changed when the next poll goes out.

faq_plan.q: What are some funny poll questions?
faq_plan.ref: What are some funny poll questions?

prov.original: What are some funny poll questions?

faq_plan.a: Here are five funny poll questions that pick on no one. Is a hot dog a sandwich? Pineapple on pizza: yes or no? Socks with sandals: crime or comfort? Would you rather lose your keys or your phone charger? Is cereal a soup? Before you post one, try your funniest poll questions on two friends and keep the ones that get an answer straight away.

faq_plan.q: How do I create poll questions?
faq_plan.a: Write one question with two to five answers, decide who may vote and when the poll closes, then share the link. In Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the poll in a sentence, and Emergent builds a voting page you can share by link. A follow-up prompt changes the question, the answers, or the closing time.

faq_plan.q: What are some fun questions to ask in a group poll?
faq_plan.ref: What are some fun questions to ask in a group poll?

prov.original: What are some fun questions to ask in a group poll?

faq_plan.a: Ask questions every member can answer without a debate. Pizza or tacos for the next get-together? Which decade had the best music? Beach week or mountain week? Early bird or night owl? Group poll questions like these are quick to answer, and some of them settle a real plan, such as where to eat next time.

faq_plan.q: What are some good poll questions?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good poll questions?

prov.original: What are some good poll questions?

faq_plan.a: Good poll questions ask about one thing and offer answers people can pick at a glance. Which day works best for the team lunch? Which of these four outings gets your vote? Was today's meeting too long or about right? Multiple choice poll questions like these end with a clear count. When you need details, such as where a repair is needed, use a work order form.

faq_plan.q: What are some fun poll questions I can ask my friends?
faq_plan.ref: What are some fun poll questions I can ask my friends?

prov.original: What are some fun poll questions I can ask my friends?

faq_plan.a: Try these fun poll questions with friends. Would you rather explore space or the deep sea? What is the best road trip snack? Which movie deserves a rewatch? Cats or dogs? Save anything that splits the group, like money or politics, for a real conversation, and keep your poll questions for fun light.

Poll questions come in a few types. This or that: Mountains or ocean? Multiple choice: Which board game goes on the shelf next? Rating: Rate this week's all-hands, 1 for wasted time and 5 for time well spent. Open: What name fits the new conference room? For a busy channel, this or that poll questions make the easiest poll of the day questions.

faq_plan.q: What are good would you rather poll questions?
faq_plan.a: Good would you rather poll questions offer two choices that are equally tempting or equally annoying. Would you rather give up coffee or dessert for a month? Would you rather always arrive 10 minutes early or 10 minutes late? Would you rather work a week from a beach or from a cabin? Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a poll like this.

faq_plan.q: Where should a website place opinion poll questions?
faq_plan.ref: a popular website places opinion poll questions
faq_plan.a: Place an opinion poll where readers have formed a view: at the end of an article, beside the topic it asks about, or on the page people see after they finish a task. Ask one question per poll. Show the results only after a vote, and keep the poll away from the content people came to read.

faq_plan.q: Which poll questions are allowed in a work chat?
faq_plan.a: Questions anyone can answer without sharing something private are fine: lunch spots, weekend plans, and this-or-that choices. Aim funny poll questions for work at shared work life, such as Monday mornings or the printer, never at a coworker. Leave out politics, religion, health, and pay. Keep fun poll questions for work optional.

faq_plan.q: How can a business make poll questions profitable?
faq_plan.a: Tie each poll to a decision that costs or earns money. Ask customers which flavor to stock next or which delivery day suits them, act on the winner, and compare sales before and after. Build the poll app with Emergent, and it can send each vote to a tool you already use, such as your CRM, through its API.

plan.angle: The top 10 for poll questions are lists: fun polls, group chat polls, would-you-rather sets, a subreddit and two Pinterest boards. None shows a poll actually running or what happens to the votes. This page shows four polls built from a prompt and run to a result: a this-or-that poll of the day in a work Slack channel, a multiple choice poll that picks a team outing, a live audience poll on a conference screen, and a would-you-rather vote that settles a friends' trip. The FAQ carries the example questions searchers want, sorted by setting, and answers the odd Semrush questions plainly as advice.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Poll Questions People Answer and Act On'; hero 'Build poll questions for work, events, or friends, and save every vote to a database you own.' covers the whole job; how-to description is one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Top 10 are example lists; FAQ carries about 25 example questions by setting (funny, group, friends, work, would you rather, types) and the how-to teaches writing good poll questions; tabs show four polls run to a result.

specificity.evidence: Poll-specific detail throughout: 'Hide the totals until the poll closes if early votes would sway others'; step 2 'Add hot or iced to the same question, and the room splits four ways'.

openers.evidence: Every body opens on a full sentence, e.g. 'At 9:00 each morning, Pellworth Freight's operations team gets one this-or-that question in Slack.'

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; 11 'A, B, and C' lists noted (QC Q8 P2).

voice.evidence: Reads human: 'Read each funny question aloud, picture the quietest person on the team hearing it, and cut any that would sting.' Two stilted reworded FAQ questions noted.

truth.evidence: Every Emergent sentence maps to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, conversational, no-caps, realtime, alerts, api-connect, custom-domain, code-export, free-start); no third-party facts in prose, only advice; tab numbers add up (22+14=36 of 48; 11+7+4+2=24 of 27; 97+45=142 of 180; 7+5=12).

distinct.evidence: Poll-specific stories (poll of the day, live audience slide) distinct from funny-survey-questions; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions answered in the first sentence; Semrush slots 7-10 keep their head phrases ('would you rather poll questions', 'opinion poll questions', 'poll questions allowed', 'poll questions profitable') and read as real questions; hub link in item 2.

images.evidence: Each tab image matches copy: coffee 22 / tea 14, 36 of 48; bowling 11, escape room 7, cooking 4, karaoke 2, 24 of 27; reply-all 97 / 7 a.m. 45, 142 of 180; cabin 7 / beach 5, 2 email reminders.
